CatalogServer.description: One MCP server of a run and the tools it offered.

name.description: The name of the server: at least one character, and unique among the servers of its snapshot.

source_digest.description: The digest of the server's source file.

source_path.description: The path of the server's source file: a POSIX path relative to the project root.

tools.$comment: Tool names are unique within the array, compared byte for byte (case-sensitive, without Unicode normalisation); JSON Schema cannot state this, and the Rust reader refuses a repeated name.
tools.description: The tools the server offered, with names unique among them.

transport.description: How a client reaches the server.

Digest.description: A content digest: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

NameToken.description: A catalog provider reference, `name@token`, split at the last `@`: the name is non-empty and holds neither `@` nor white space, and the token matches `[0-9A-Za-z.+-]+`.

RelPath.description: A run-relative POSIX path: non-empty, with no leading `/`, no empty segment, no `.` or `..` segment, no NUL and no `\`.

Timestamp.$comment: The pattern states the lexical form; a date or time that names no instant, such as month 13, and a fraction of more than nine digits are refused by the parser.
Timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp with an uppercase `T` and an explicit offset, `Z` or `±HH:MM`.

Tool.description: A tool in MCP `tools/list` shape: the named keys of the MCP `Tool` definition, and every other key as the server gave it.

annotations.description: Hints about the behaviour of the tool: an open object whose keys are kept as given.

description.description: A human-readable description of the tool.

inputSchema.description: The JSON Schema object that describes the arguments of the tool. Its `type` is not required to be `object`.

name.description: The name of the tool, as the server gave it: at least one character, and unique among the tools of its server.

outputSchema.description: The JSON Schema object that describes the structured output of the tool.

title.description: A human-readable title of the tool.

Transport.description: How a client reaches an MCP server.

oneOf.description: The server runs as a subprocess and is spoken to over its standard input and output.
The server is reached over streamable HTTP.
The server is reached over server-sent events.

description: What the MCP servers targeted by a run offered: for each server, its tools in the shape of an MCP `tools/list` result.

environment.description: The versions the capture depended on, as an object from a name to its version text.

ext.description: Provider-specific data: an open JSON object that Candler does not interpret.

provider.description: The catalog provider that captured the snapshot, as `name@token`.

schema.description: The version marker of the document: always `tool-catalog-snapshot/1`.

servers.$comment: Server names are unique within the array, compared byte for byte (case-sensitive, without Unicode normalisation); JSON Schema cannot state this, and the Rust reader refuses a repeated name.
servers.description: The servers the run targeted, each with the tools it offered, with names unique among them.

title: CatalogSnapshot
